pr_body:
Fixes #12635

As discussed in the issue, supporting the set0-like semantics long-term is not necessarily desirable, although necessary for short-term compatibility concerns. So I've deprecated the original method and added an equivalent that is explicitly labelled as set1.

I tried to audit existing usages of the (now-deprecated) API and update them to use set1 if that appeared to align with their expectations.

- [x] documentation is added or updated
- [x] tests are added or updated

issue_context.title: Memory leak of BIGNUM related to EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_rsa_keygen_pubexp() changes in 3.0.0
issue_context.body:
I started seeing complaints of a BIGNUM leak while running a testcase involving RSA key generation under ASAN against 3.0.0-alpha6.

EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_rsa_keygen_pubexp() no longer appears to take custody of the BIGNUM passed onto it. Presumably this is an artifact of the transition to the provider model. (I imagine doing copies before passing data off to the providers is quite typical and makes good sense from the internal POV.)

A few key points:

1. The documentation still states, "The pubexp pointer is used internally by this function so it should not be modified or freed after the call." As far as I can tell that does not square with the new behavior.
 
2. Changing memory custody semantics for pre-existing APIs is probably leaving a land mine for applications, particularly when those semantics were in fact explicitly defined (see 1). It will be very easy for existing applications to begin leaking memory after updating libraries.
 
3. It seems quite plausible to me that this isn't the only EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_* API with such an impact. I'm not explicitly aware of any others, so perhaps the bug is unique. However, the circumstances seem somewhat generic, and hence my concern.
comments:
Due to the existing semantics we would basically need to release the BIGNUM once we copy it into the provider. 

The question is - could there be existing applications than would be "surprised" by the immediate release of the BIGNUM and expecting that although they cannot modify the BIGNUM anymore after that call with the existing contract that they expect to be able to use it in a read-only way? I hope we can ignore this corner case.

The current behavior is especially goofy. Looks like in the "legacy" case, it behaves as in 1.1.1, taking ownership, while the provider case, it copies. That means a caller needs to either predict which path will be used, or risk either a leak or a UAF.

There aren't any perfect answers here, but I think releasing the object is the way to go. That's what we've done in BoringSSL in other cases where we've had to retain compatibility with a `set0`-like function but have since changed the internal representation. Sadly, in some edge cases, callers may be relying on the object to still be around, despite having relinquished ownership of it. I think this is, strictly speaking, incompatible with the notion of relinquishing ownership, but folks do it. It's fairly rare and you can usually fix the caller, but not a great situation.

Another option is to have the `EVP_PKEY_CTX` own a placeholder `BIGNUM` object, retained solely for callers' benefit. And then either have one of these for each property, or one per type and only retain the `BIGNUM` for the most recent API called. (On grounds that, if you relinquish ownership *and* mutate the parent object, you *really* don't have grounds to assume the object is alive.) But this is very hacky, so we've usually opted to just fix the few affected callers. (Usually a matter of bumping a refcount or reordering some lines.)

This is the nuisance with non-copying `get0` and `set0` API. :-( They avoid the copy, which is nice, but they implicitly constrain the implementation.

So the safest way would be to have the copy of all the BIGNUMs in the library context AND deprecate the APIs which require the copy so we could eventually drop them in a future API breaking release. Not sure if we need to do it or that we can just say that even read-only use after set0 is a misuse of the API. Unfortunately we do not have the BoringSSL advantage of having only known callers - there might be simply just anything out there and use-after-free bugs can be quite ugly.

>have the copy of all the BIGNUMs in the library context AND deprecate the APIs

Why in the library context? Why not take a copy in the EVP_PKEY_CTX?
By the library context I've meant the EVP_PKEY_CTX in the library. I'm sorry for not being clear.

review_comments: Please can you add an entry to CHANGES.md explaining that this is now deprecated and that the preferred alternative is EVP_PKEY_CTX_set1_rsa_keygen_pubexp().

Why? The original code frees the local BIGNUM only in the event an error is returned, which makes sense because in the success case the set0-style API took over custody. Because I changed to set1-style, where a copy is always made, the local BIGNUM should always be freed afterward. I don't see how the code you've cited has anything to do with it.

Was just making sure you were aware of that path..
The free still does a BN_free(rctx->pub_exp).. so it should be ok.

Should it be doing the dup in here or in the ctrl?

```
ret = EVP_PKEY_CTX_ctrl(ctx, EVP_PKEY_RSA, EVP_PKEY_OP_KEYGEN,
                                          EVP_PKEY_CTRL_RSA_KEYGEN_PUBEXP,
                                          copy, pubexp);
```

EVP_PKEY_CTX_ctrl() is technically a public API, right? So changing behavior there to do a copy instead of "taking custody" as it currently does would kind of be introducing into another API the same exact issue this change is trying to solve: preexisting callers who expect that they are no longer responsible for freeing the BIGNUM once it has been "passed off" to the API would suddenly start leaking memory.
